recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-29557 unless BR&R later reopens the top-level packaging cardinality.
issue_request: FHIR-29557 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request for R5 asking to correct top-level PackagedProductDefinition.package from 0..* to 0..1 because there can be only one package layer at the top of the package tree.
initial_application: The request was applied in commit 342df35139006b3e71d2ddcbbcc16860ebc2fdb1, which changed the then-authoritative PackagedProductDefinition spreadsheet row from 0..* to 0..1 for FHIR#29557. Later source rework replaced the spreadsheet with StructureDefinition XML while preserving the 0..1 rule.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists PackagedProductDefinition as an active draft BR&R resource, and the current source defines the renamed PackagedProductDefinition.packaging element with min 0 and max 1. FHIR-29692 later renamed PackageProductDefinition.package to PackagedProductDefinition.packaging, explaining why the issue's original path now appears under the packaging name. Confluence BR&R minutes confirm the original 24-0-0 cardinality motion, and no community search results conflicted with the current source.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. The old PackagedProductDefinition.package path is absent from active PackagedProductDefinition source, examples use one top-level packaging element with nested packaging for inner layers, and no source hunk was necessary.
